href=\"learning-bibliography.html#bibliography-use\">How these sources were used<\/a><\/div><\/details><\/div><\/details><\/aside><div id=\"navBackdrop\" class=\"nav-backdrop\"><\/div><div class=\"page-frame report-frame\"><main class=\"shell report curriculum-report\" id=\"mainContent\">\n<div class=\"section-guide-band\"><h1 id=\"curriculum-title\">Curriculum design<\/h1><div class=\"page-avatar-slot\"><div id=\"avatarWrap\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><\/div><\/div><\/div><p class=\"report-lead\">The decisions behind the learning journey.<\/p><p>I began with an ordinary material and a question worth investigating: what can we find out about sticks, and how confidently can we use that evidence? I developed a four-lesson sequence for 15-year-old learners, then reconsidered the outcomes, progression and assessment for first-year undergraduates.<\/p><p>The topic stays familiar. The learning changes: from observing and planning a fair comparison to analysing measurements and judging the limits of a physical model. This section explains the choices behind that progression and links directly to the teaching evidence.<\/p><p class=\"curriculum-status\">This is a working curriculum sketch for a fictional brief. The resources and prototypes can be inspected; classroom delivery, institutional approval and learning impact still need to be tested.<\/p>\n<div class=\"section-guide-actions\"><details><summary id=\"sectionGuideRead\">Read spoken introduction<\/summary><p id=\"sectionGuideTranscript\"><\/p><\/details><\/div><nav class=\"curriculum-contents\" aria-label=\"Curriculum section contents\"><p>Choose a heading to follow the reasoning, or open the teaching materials to inspect a decision in practice.<\/p><ol><li><a href=\"#curriculum-brief\">Start with the need and the intended learning<\/a><\/li><li><a href=\"#curriculum-outcomes\">Connect outcomes, activities and evidence<\/a><\/li><li><a href=\"#curriculum-sequence\">Sequence the learning, not just the content<\/a><\/li><li><a href=\"#curriculum-assessment\">Use assessment to guide and judge learning<\/a><\/li><li><a href=\"#curriculum-access\">Vary the support; preserve the purpose<\/a><\/li><li><a href=\"#curriculum-delivery\">Design for the tutor and the institution too<\/a><\/li><li><a href=\"#curriculum-ai\">Give AI a bounded role<\/a><\/li><li><a href=\"#curriculum-evaluation\">Evaluate the journey and revise it<\/a><\/li><\/ol><\/nav>\n<section aria-labelledby=\"curriculum-brief\"><h2 id=\"curriculum-brief\">Start with the need and the intended learning<\/h2><p>I treated the brief as a learning problem before treating it as a collection of lessons. The starting point was “Sticks: How to explore stick characteristics”. That became a sequence in which learners ask a testable question, gather evidence, interpret it and make a recommendation they can defend.<\/p><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>What I know, and what I would establish first<\/summary><div><p>The project defines two audiences and supplies a practical context. It does not establish their actual prior knowledge, access needs or institutional constraints. I would use diagnostic tasks, discussion with tutors and learner feedback to establish those before delivery.<\/p><p>For the school route, I would check measurement, units, variables and the language of scientific explanation. For the undergraduate route, I would add SI conversions, graph gradients, algebra and the distinction between stiffness, modulus and strength. Age identifies a route; it does not tell me everything about the person using it.<\/p><p>I would also establish available teaching time, apparatus, tutor capacity, approved assessment requirements and the support needed to participate. Those findings could change the plan, rather than simply confirm it.<\/p><\/div><\/details><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>Make curriculum alignment explicit and provisional<\/summary><div><p>The age-15 pack uses England’s Key Stage 4 science programme, particularly Working scientifically, as a provisional reference. The stick investigation is a context for those skills, not a separately prescribed unit. I would check the relevant local curriculum and examination specification.<\/p><p>The undergraduate pack proposes first-year outcomes in experimental design, quantitative analysis and critical evaluation. Those require mapping to the actual module and programme before adoption. Suggested workload and assessment weightings are planning decisions, not institutional regulations.<\/p><p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-school-pack.html#heading-6\">Inspect the school outcomes and curriculum connections →<\/a><\/p><p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-university-pack.html#heading-4\">Inspect the undergraduate outcomes and programme mapping →<\/a><\/p><\/div><\/details><\/section>\n<section aria-labelledby=\"curriculum-outcomes\"><h2 id=\"curriculum-outcomes\">Connect outcomes, activities and evidence<\/h2><p>I work backwards from what learners should be able to demonstrate. An activity earns its place when it helps develop an intended outcome and produces evidence that a tutor can interpret. The question is not simply whether a task is engaging, but what understanding it makes visible.<\/p><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>Age 15: a fair investigation and a qualified explanation<\/summary><div><p>Learners describe and compare observable characteristics, measure with appropriate units, form a testable hypothesis, identify variables, collect and graph results, and explain limitations. The final recommendation must refer to their evidence.<\/p><p>For example, the outcome “present results and explain whether they support the hypothesis” leads to repeated displacement readings, a results table, an appropriate graph and an individual explanation. The teacher checks the reasoning, not just whether the graph looks complete.<\/p><p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-school-pack.html#heading-17\">Follow the school outcomes into the assessment criteria →<\/a><\/p><\/div><\/details><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>Undergraduate: a reproducible method and a defensible model<\/summary><div><p>Learners characterise irregular specimens, justify sampling and controls, analyse force–deflection data, address uncertainty and judge whether a model supports the conclusion. A calculation is part of the evidence, rather than the whole outcome.<\/p><p>For example, estimating specimen stiffness requires traceable measurements, SI calculations and an explained force–deflection relationship. An apparent modulus also requires defensible geometry and model assumptions. If those assumptions are not supported, reporting stiffness with appropriate limitations may be the better conclusion.<\/p><p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-university-pack.html#heading-24\">Inspect the analysis worksheet and simulated practice data →<\/a><\/p><p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-university-pack.html#heading-34\">Inspect the report criteria and oral check →<\/a><\/p><\/div><\/details><\/section>\n<section aria-labelledby=\"curriculum-sequence\"><h2 id=\"curriculum-sequence\">Sequence the learning, not just the content<\/h2><p>I arranged the work so that each stage prepares learners for the next decision. Observation precedes the hypothesis; method approval precedes practical work; analysis precedes a recommendation. This reduces the risk of asking for sophisticated conclusions before learners have the evidence or concepts to support them.<\/p><h3 id=\"curriculum-school-journey\">Age 15 · four 60-minute lessons<\/h3><div class=\"curriculum-journey\"><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>1 · Observe and compare<\/summary><div><p>Start with contrasting sticks, descriptive vocabulary and measurement. Learners move from everyday impressions to recorded observations of length, diameter, mass and condition. A short check distinguishes observation from inference.<\/p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-school-pack.html#heading-22\">Open Lesson 1 →<\/a><\/div><\/details><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>2 · Predict and plan<\/summary><div><p>Turn an observation into a testable question about diameter and bending. Learners identify the variables, plan consistent support spacing and loading, and recognise differences such as moisture and condition. The tutor reviews the method before practical work.<\/p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-school-pack.html#heading-29\">Open Lesson 2 →<\/a><\/div><\/details><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>3 · Investigate and analyse<\/summary><div><p>Use a teacher-approved setup and small loads, repeat readings and organise results. Learners construct a graph, look for patterns and discuss unexpected results. Repeated readings on one stick are distinguished from testing additional independent sticks.<\/p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-school-pack.html#heading-36\">Open Lesson 3 →<\/a><\/div><\/details><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>4 · Evaluate and apply<\/summary><div><p>Judge how well the evidence supports the hypothesis, explain at least two limitations and propose improvements. Apply the findings to a model-structure recommendation, with individual reasoning and peer feedback.<\/p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-school-pack.html#heading-43\">Open Lesson 4 →<\/a><\/div><\/details><\/div><h3 id=\"curriculum-university-journey\">Undergraduate · four two-hour sessions<\/h3><p>The university pack also allows approximately six hours of independent reading, analysis and reporting. Those timings would need piloting with the intended cohort.<\/p><div class=\"curriculum-journey\"><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>1 · Characterisation and theory<\/summary><div><p>Establish units, gradients and the distinction between stiffness and strength. Record specimen geometry and condition before introducing the ideal beam assumptions. The output is a traceable specimen log and a question worth testing.<\/p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-university-pack.html#heading-14\">Open Session 1 →<\/a><\/div><\/details><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>2 · Protocol design and pilot<\/summary><div><p>Audit a flawed protocol, justify controls and distinguish independent specimens from technical repeats. Pilot the approved procedure, then revise the method and recording plan before collecting the main dataset.<\/p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-university-pack.html#heading-16\">Open Session 2 →<\/a><\/div><\/details><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>3 · Measurement and quantitative analysis<\/summary><div><p>Collect traceable data, fit an appropriate relationship, inspect residuals and consider uncertainty. Learners explain the limits of any stiffness or apparent-modulus estimate rather than treating a good fit as model validation.<\/p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-university-pack.html#heading-18\">Open Session 3 →<\/a><\/div><\/details><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>4 · Scientific critique and design application<\/summary><div><p>Defend a conclusion, audit claims and make a limited design recommendation. Peer review and an individual oral check test the reasoning behind the report, including a decision or limitation that could change its interpretation.<\/p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-university-pack.html#heading-20\">Open Session 4 →<\/a><\/div><\/details><\/div><p class=\"curriculum-note\">The digital activities provide practice, feedback and a way to inspect the design. They complement the teaching packs and practical investigation; operating a model alone does not demonstrate practical competence.<\/p><\/section>\n<section aria-labelledby=\"curriculum-assessment\"><h2 id=\"curriculum-assessment\">Use assessment to guide and judge learning<\/h2><p>I use assessment at the beginning, during the work and at the end, with a different purpose at each point. The evidence should help the teacher decide what to do next as well as support a judgement about achievement.<\/p><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>Diagnose and give feedback before the final task<\/summary><div><p>Opening predictions expose assumptions that the teaching can revisit. During the sequence, method checks, questions, data reviews, exit tickets and peer critique reveal where explanation or practice is needed. These checks are opportunities to adjust support, not simply accumulate marks.<\/p><p>The prototypes automatically check bounded practice answers. Written reasoning still needs tutor review. A score on a mean or stiffness calculation cannot establish whether a learner can plan an investigation or defend a conclusion.<\/p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-school-pack.html#heading-13\">Inspect the school assessment sequence →<\/a><\/div><\/details><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>Gather individual evidence and keep scores meaningful<\/summary><div><p>The age-15 final task is a short investigation report or equivalent recorded presentation with data, a graph, a conclusion, limitations and a recommendation. The rubric awards 0–3 across five criteria, giving 15 marks. The separate 10-mark knowledge check is reported separately; these are not GCSE grade boundaries.<\/p><p>The undergraduate task is an individual 1,500-word report with data and calculation appendices, plus an oral check or approved equivalent. The suggested weighting is 90% report and 10% oral check, subject to local module rules.<\/p><p>Group measurements can be shared when their provenance and contributions are clear. Analysis, interpretation and evaluation must still demonstrate each learner’s understanding. The tutor dashboards show fictional submissions and review mechanisms, not validated automated marking or measured learning gains.<\/p><p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-school-pack.html#heading-85\">Inspect the school marking rubric →<\/a><\/p><p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-university-pack.html#heading-34\">Inspect the undergraduate assessment brief →<\/a><\/p><\/div><\/details><\/section>\n<section aria-labelledby=\"curriculum-access\"><h2 id=\"curriculum-access\">Vary the support; preserve the purpose<\/h2><p>Differentiation changes the route into the thinking, not just the amount of work. I use evidence of readiness and participation to decide which support to provide, reduce or extend.<\/p><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>Build access into the learning route<\/summary><div><p>School resources include vocabulary prompts, sentence starters, recording tables and graph scaffolds. Undergraduates can use unit-conversion examples, a protocol template or a scaffolded spreadsheet alongside an open analysis route. Language choices and readable instructions support access to the task, while scientific meaning and evidence requirements remain consistent.<\/p><p>Flexible practical roles, accessible apparatus and recorded explanations can remove unnecessary barriers. An alternative response format should still demonstrate the intended outcome. If simulated data replace practical access, practical competence needs separate evidence.<\/p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-school-pack.html#heading-18\">Inspect differentiation and access in the school pack →<\/a><\/div><\/details><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>Extend the reasoning rather than add routine work<\/summary><div><p>Extensions ask learners to examine sampling, confounding variables, geometry sensitivity, uncertainty or competing models. The challenge is a better justified decision, not merely a longer worksheet. I would reduce scaffolding when the evidence shows readiness and restore it when an unfamiliar demand creates a barrier.<\/p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-university-pack.html#heading-10\">Inspect undergraduate support and extension →<\/a><\/div><\/details><\/section>\n<section aria-labelledby=\"curriculum-delivery\"><h2 id=\"curriculum-delivery\">Design for the tutor and the institution too<\/h2><p>A curriculum has to work for the people who teach, support and approve it. I developed lesson plans, student resources, marking guidance and tutor views together so the intended journey can be followed beyond the learner’s screen.<\/p><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>Make preparation, delivery and review workable<\/summary><div><p>The tutor needs a clear sequence, preparation notes, timing, apparatus checks, approved procedures and a way to respond to misconceptions. Practical work uses inspected samples and small approved loads; learners do not deliberately load sticks to breaking point. Less bending does not establish a safe failure load.<\/p><p>The institution needs alignment with its outcomes, assessment and access arrangements, a feasible workload, responsibilities for updates and an agreed submission process. I would establish what progress information is needed and who should see it before collecting it.<\/p><p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-school-pack.html#heading-54\">Inspect teacher preparation →<\/a><\/p><p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-university-pack.html#heading-8\">Inspect laboratory preparation and model assumptions →<\/a><\/p><\/div><\/details><\/section>\n<section aria-labelledby=\"curriculum-ai\"><h2 id=\"curriculum-ai\">Give AI a bounded role<\/h2><p>I used generative AI to help draft resources, consider alternative explanations and develop critique tasks, then directed revisions around the learning outcomes and evidence. It supports the development process; it does not validate the science, the assessment or the learner’s achievement.<\/p><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>Match AI use to the audience and learning purpose<\/summary><div><p>The school route uses teacher-mediated resources and checked flawed examples; it does not require students to hold an AI account. The undergraduate route can include approved AI critique or coding support, with disclosure and independent verification. A non-AI alternative remains available.<\/p><p>Both routes ask learners to challenge claims using evidence. Generated references, formulas, calculations and explanations need checking. Fabricated data and invented citations cannot become evidence because an answer sounds plausible.<\/p><p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-university-pack.html#heading-30\">Inspect the AI claim audit and design challenge →<\/a><\/p><p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-ai-development.html#page-heading\">Read the separate account of AI in web development →<\/a><\/p><\/div><\/details><\/section>\n<section aria-labelledby=\"curriculum-evaluation\"><h2 id=\"curriculum-evaluation\">Evaluate the journey and revise it<\/h2><p>The curriculum rationale is an argument to test. I would review whether learners achieve each outcome, where the sequence creates difficulty and whether the available time and support are sufficient.<\/p><details class=\"curriculum-fold\"><summary>Collect evidence that can change the next version<\/summary><div><p>Before delivery, I would check content and calculations, pilot apparatus and workload, and review accessibility with representative users and tutors. During delivery, I would inspect questions, plans, raw-data quality, participation and the explanations learners give.<\/p><p>After delivery, I would compare entry and exit responses, review individual work against the rubric, moderate marking and gather learner and tutor feedback. I would identify which instruction, example, scaffold or stage needs changing, record the reason and test the revision.<\/p><p>Polished resources, completed answer boxes and fictional dashboard scores are evidence of a working prototype. They are not evidence that understanding has improved. That distinction keeps the next development decision tied to what we actually know.<\/p><a class=\"curriculum-evidence-link\" href=\"learning-university-pack.html#heading-42\">Inspect the teaching evaluation and future plan →<\/a><\/div><\/details><p>Curriculum design sets the intended learning journey. Two deliberately different learning experiences.<\/h2><p>The purpose is to show how I turn a shared subject into learning that suits different starting points, rather than merely changing the wording. Investigating sticks provides an accessible practical context. The school pathway develops observation, measurement, fair testing and evidence-based explanation. The university pathway adds quantitative modelling, uncertainty, independent analysis and criticism of assumptions.<\/p><h3>The learning design process<\/h3><p>I began with the audience, likely prior knowledge, intended outcomes and practical constraints. I then aligned each outcome with an activity and observable evidence of understanding. The sequence moves from examining specimens to planning, investigation, interpretation and application. Neither a polished interface nor a correct objective answer proves learning effectiveness. Evaluation should examine individual reasoning, accessibility, practical performance and transfer to a new problem.<\/p><h3>Learning design, curriculum and access<\/h3><p>I selected a familiar, low-cost material to make the intellectual task accessible without making the reasoning trivial. The curriculum emphasis is scientific enquiry: distinguishing a measurement from an inference, a fair comparison from a causal claim, and stiffness from breaking strength. Local subject specifications must be checked before treating these examples as a mapped unit.<\/p><p>I use a diagnostic starting point, a worked example, guided practice and an independent explanation. The support can be increased or faded in response to evidence; age does not prescribe ability. Discussion develops vocabulary and reasoning, but an individual response is needed to reveal what each learner understands.<\/p><p>Content is chunked around meaningful decisions rather than arbitrary screen lengths. Each explanation places its next action alongside the text. Stable breadcrumbs, a persistent header, clear active choices and one main scroll area reduce avoidable navigation effort. Revise entre compañeros y obtenga aprobación docente. Especie, humedad, nudos y estado pueden confundir la comparación. Repetir lecturas no equivale a añadir muestras independientes.<\/p><h3>Clase 3 · Investigar y analizar · 60 minutos<\/h3><p>Siga el procedimiento aprobado, registre lecturas con y sin carga y calcule su diferencia. Compruebe la recuperación al retirar la carga antes de repetir. Mantenga constantes las condiciones acordadas. Calcule la media de las lecturas válidas y represente diámetro en el eje horizontal y desplazamiento medio en el vertical, con unidades y escalas regulares. No una los puntos por orden de muestra ni elimine un resultado solo porque contradice la predicción. Si el tiempo no basta, reduzca el número de muestras o separe la sesión de gráficos tras probar la carga de trabajo.<\/p><h3>Clase 4 · Evaluar y aplicar · 60 minutos<\/h3><p>Determine si las pruebas apoyan la hipótesis. Cite al menos dos resultados, explique dos limitaciones y una mejora relacionada para cada una. Recomiende muestras para miembros de un pequeño puente de maqueta con una luz indicada por el docente. Incluya un boceto y nuevas pruebas necesarias: uniones, configuración, cargas repetidas y resistencia a la rotura. La recomendación no demuestra capacidad de carga ni seguridad del puente.<\/p><h3>Hojas de trabajo esenciales<\/h3><p>Registro: muestra; longitud; diámetro; masa; textura; estado; observaciones. Plan: pregunta; hipótesis; variable comparada; resultado medido; controles; método; factores no controlados; condiciones de parada; aprobación. Resultados: muestra; diámetro en mm; desplazamientos 1, 2 y 3 en mm; media. Registre también luz, carga total y tiempo de lectura.<\/p><p>Media = suma de desplazamientos válidos ÷ número de lecturas válidas. Ejemplo simulado: (4 + 5 + 3) ÷ 3 = 4 mm. No copie datos simulados como resultados experimentales. Una menor flexión en condiciones equivalentes indica mayor resistencia a la flexión en ese montaje, no mayor carga de rotura.<\/p><h3>Actividades de razonamiento<\/h3><p>Clasifique observaciones, inferencias y predicciones. Ejemplos: «la balanza indica 24 g» es una observación; «puede contener más humedad» es una inferencia; «con la misma carga se doblará menos» es una predicción. Audite un plan que usa distinta carga y separación entre apoyos para palos gruesos y finos. Corrija controles, lecturas, muestreo y la conclusión errónea de que el que menos se dobla es siempre el más resistente.<\/p><h3>Evaluación y respuestas<\/h3><p>Producto final individual: pregunta e hipótesis, método y variables, tabla y gráfico, conclusión con resultados, dos limitaciones y mejoras, y recomendación justificada. Puede utilizar datos de grupo, pero la explicación debe ser individual; una presentación grabada equivalente conserva las mismas exigencias.<\/p><p>Prueba separada de 10 puntos: resultado medido y unidad, 2; dos controles, 2; media de 3, 4 y 5 mm, 1; diferencia entre repetición y muestras independientes, 2; diferencia entre flexión y rotura, 1; limitación y mejora relacionada, 2. Respuestas: desplazamiento vertical del punto medio en mm; controles como luz y carga; media de 4 mm; las repeticiones informan de consistencia, las muestras independientes de variación entre muestras; no se midió la carga de rotura.<\/p><p>Rúbrica de investigación: cinco criterios, de 0 a 3 puntos cada uno, total 15: observación y medición; planificación; análisis; conclusión y aplicación; evaluación. 0: sin evidencia pertinente. 1: evidencia parcial o inconsistente. 2: evidencia clara y mayoritariamente correcta. 3: evidencia precisa, justificada y con límites explícitos, según los descriptores originales. Informe los 15 puntos y la prueba de 10 por separado; no son límites de calificación GCSE validados.<\/p><h3>Apoyo, IA y evaluación de la enseñanza<\/h3><p>Use vocabulario visual, ejemplos, tablas guiadas, escalas sugeridas y respuestas orales cuando proceda. Amplíe mediante resolución instrumental, variación y diseños que controlen factores de confusión. La IA manejada por el docente puede ayudar a redactar recursos y ejemplos deliberadamente erróneos, siempre revisados y etiquetados; no se requieren cuentas del alumnado. Compruebe afirmaciones científicas y no suba trabajos identificables. Tras impartir, revise respuestas iniciales y finales, trabajos, participación, tiempos y accesibilidad. No se han medido aún resultados de aprendizaje ni ahorro de tiempo.<\/p>\", \"university\": \"<h2>Guía docente en español: primer curso universitario<\/h2><p><strong>Edición concisa traducida.<\/strong> Conserva los conceptos, la secuencia, el ejemplo numérico y los criterios centrales. Se presuponen álgebra básica, unidades SI y gráficos; la teoría especializada se introduce en la unidad. Cuatro sesiones de dos horas más unas seis horas autónomas. No deduzca seguridad estructural ni carga de rotura a partir de este ensayo.<\/p><h3>Registro y ejemplo simulado<\/h3><p>Conserve identificación de muestra y ciclo, masa añadida, fuerza, desplazamiento, carga/descarga y tiempo. \"<h2>中文教学指南：十五岁学生<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>本版介绍主要课程顺序、概念和评估，并非下方完整英语工作表及评分描述的逐项翻译。<\/p><h3>目标与成果<\/h3><p>探究树枝特征与其表现之间的关系。学生应能描述至少四项特征；使用适当单位测量长度、直径和质量；提出可检验假设；识别变量；实施教师批准的探究；作图；说明两项局限及相应改进。暂以英格兰第四关键阶段科学探究要求为参考，实施时须对照本校实际课程。<\/p><h3>准备与安全<\/h3><p>准备已编号和检查的试样、尺、天平、可用的卡尺、稳定支架及记录表。剔除尖锐、开裂起刺或发霉试样。教师须预先测试跨距和小载荷，使弯曲可测且不造成损坏。不得以折断为目标。手和脸应远离试验区；发现开裂声、滑动或永久变形时立即停止。使用预先收集的材料，避免破坏栖息地。<\/p><h3>第一课：观察与比较，六十分钟<\/h3><p>0–8分钟：描述两根树枝并预测表现。8–16分钟：区分观察与推断，介绍词汇。16–25分钟：示范测量、单位和精度。25–45分钟：检查至少四个试样，轮换测量、记录、器材和核查角色。45–55分钟：比较结果并提出可检验问题。55–60分钟：提交一项观察、一项推断及一项带单位的测量。<\/p><h3>第二课：预测与计划，六十分钟<\/h3><p>核心问题：固定载荷下，直径与弯曲有何关系？将位移定义为中点相对无载位置的垂直移动。确定编号、直径测量位置、跨距、总载荷、加载位置、试样方向、读数时间及重复次数。互评后获得教师批准。树种、含水量、节疤和状态可能混杂比较。重复读取同一试样不等于增加独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三课：探究与分析，六十分钟<\/h3><p>按批准方案记录加载与无载读数并求差。卸载后检查是否恢复，再重复。保持约定条件一致。对有效读数求平均，以直径为横轴、平均位移为纵轴绘制散点图，标注单位并采用均匀刻度。不要按试样顺序连点，也不要仅因结果不符合预测而删除它。若时间不足，应先试行工作量，再减少样本或另设作图时间。<\/p><h3>第四课：评价与应用，六十分钟<\/h3><p>判断证据是否支持假设，引用至少两项结果，说明两项局限及各自改进。为教师指定跨距的小型模型桥构件推荐试样，附示意图，并提出接头、结构布局、重复加载和破坏强度等后续试验。推荐不等于已证明承载能力或桥梁安全。<\/p><h3>核心工作表<\/h3><p>观察记录：试样、长度、直径、质量、纹理、状态和观察。计划：问题、假设、比较变量、测量结果、控制条件、方法、无法控制的因素、停止条件和批准。结果表：试样、直径（毫米）、三次位移（毫米）及平均值；另记跨距、总载荷和读数时间。<\/p><p>平均值＝有效位移读数之和÷有效次数。仅作模拟示例：(4＋5＋3)÷3＝4毫米。不能把模拟数字当作实验结果。在可比条件下弯曲较少，说明该装置下抗弯更强，并不证明断裂载荷更高。<\/p><h3>推理活动<\/h3><p>将陈述分为观察、推断和预测。例如“天平显示24克”是观察；“它可能含水更多”是推断；“相同载荷下它会弯曲更少”是预测。审查一个对粗细树枝使用不同跨距和载荷的错误计划，修正控制条件、读数次数和抽样，并纠正“弯曲最少就总是最结实”的结论。<\/p><h3>评估与答案<\/h3><p>个人成果应包括问题与假设、方法和变量、结果表与图、引用数据的结论、两项局限及改进、以及有依据的建议。可以共享小组数据，但解释必须独立。等效录音展示应保持相同科学要求。<\/p><p>另设十分知识检查：测量结果与单位2分；两个控制条件2分；3、4、5毫米平均值1分；重复与独立试样的区别2分；弯曲与破坏的区别1分；局限及相应改进2分。答案要点：中点垂直位移，毫米等长度单位；跨距和总载荷等控制条件；平均4毫米；重复反映一致性，独立试样反映试样间差异；未测断裂载荷。<\/p><p>探究量规共十五分，五个标准各0–3分：观察与测量、计划、分析、结论与应用、评价。0分表示无相关证据；1分为不完整或不一致；2分为清楚且大体正确；3分为准确、有论证且明确局限，具体以原始描述为准。十五分探究与十分检查分开报告，不能把总分当作经验证的GCSE等级界线。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与教学评价<\/h3><p>提供图示词汇、例题、引导表格、建议坐标刻度及适当口头回答方式。拓展可涉及仪器分辨率、变异和控制混杂因素的更强设计。教师可用人工智能起草资料和明确标注的错误示例，但必须核查；学生无需人工智能账户。不要上传可识别个人的作业。实施后查看起始与结束回答、作品、参与、时间和无障碍表现。目前尚未测得学习成效或备课时间节省。<\/p>\", \"<h2>中文教学指南：大学一年级<\/h2><p><strong>简明翻译版。<\/strong>保留核心概念、课程顺序、数值示例和评估标准。下方保留完整英语原版。<\/p><h3>目标与准备<\/h3><p>通过力—位移测量、分析和有限推断，探究树枝作为天然结构材料的表现。假定具备基础代数、国际单位制和作图能力；专门理论在课程中介绍。安排四次两小时课程，另加约六小时自主学习。先检查单位换算、斜率及刚度与破坏强度的区别。试验前，教师必须批准装置、步骤、载荷限制和停止条件。<\/p><h3>模型与局限<\/h3><p>理想中央加载三点弯曲模型：δ＝FL³/(48EI)；k＝dF/dδ；圆截面I＝πd⁴/64；E_app＝kL³/(48I)。区分试样及装置刚度k、材料模量E、抗弯刚度EI和破坏强度。E_app依赖几何、支承、材料和小变形假设；条件不足时仅报告k。锥度、椭圆截面、各向异性、含水量和节疤不能简单当作随机测量噪声。<\/p><h3>第一次课程：表征与理论<\/h3><p>0–15分钟诊断；15–35分钟介绍模型及SI计算；35–70分钟编号并记录质量、长度，以及三个位置各两个垂直方向直径、状态和方向；70–85分钟休息并整理几何；85–105分钟比较试样和假设，区分测量不确定度与生物变异；105–120分钟批判“越粗总是越强”，提交问题和抽样理由。<\/p><h3>第二次课程：方案与试验<\/h3><p>0–15分钟复核假设；15–35分钟审查缺陷方案；35–60分钟设计固定跨距的加载卸载、读数时间和可追溯记录；60–70分钟休息及教师审核；70–100分钟在批准范围内试验，检查分辨率、重复性及恢复；100–120分钟修订方案、分析与排除标准。明确控制条件、独立试样和技术重复。同一试样十个循环不等于十个独立试样。<\/p><h3>第三次课程：测量与分析<\/h3><p>0–10分钟确认设备与限制；10–50分钟采集独立试样数据并适当重复；50–60分钟检查数据完整性；60–85分钟用SI绘制F对δ图，对合理线性范围进行含截距拟合，检查残差及加载卸载差异；85–105分钟估计k及有依据的E_app，分开讨论测量敏感性和试样差异；105–120分钟互评并写有限结论。不得无理由强制零截距，不应隐藏滞回、漂移或残余变形。<\/p><h3>第四次课程：批判与应用<\/h3><p>0–20分钟展示图及局限；20–40分钟核查对照结论的证据与假设；40–65分钟结合刚度、质量和不确定度推荐模型桥构件；65–75分钟休息并准备报告结构；75–100分钟互评；100–115分钟个人口头检查或获批等效形式；115–120分钟提交修改重点和人工智能声明。不能由本试验推断整桥安全或断裂载荷。<\/p><h3>记录与模拟算例<\/h3><p>保留试样和循环编号、添加质量、力、位移、加载或卸载及时间。另记仪器分辨率、零点、附件质量、方向、偏离方案和修正。保留原始数据并说明小组贡献。<\/p><p>单个理想试样的模拟数据：力为0、1、2、3、4牛，位移为0、0.20、0.40、0.60、0.80毫米。L＝0.200米，d＝0.0060米。结果：k＝5牛/毫米＝5000牛/米；I≈6.36×10⁻¹¹米⁴；E_app≈1.31×10¹⁰帕＝13.1吉帕。这些是构造数据，不是实验观察或独立重复。完美直线不能估计真实噪声，也不能验证物理模型。<\/p><h3>不确定度与批判判断<\/h3><p>在圆截面模型、小且相互独立的标准不确定度条件下：u(E)/E≈√[(u(k)/k)²＋(3u(L)/L)²＋(4u(d)/d)²]。直径2%的不确定度单独贡献约8%的模量相对不确定度。此传播式不包含模型偏差、锥度、各向异性或未知含水量。高R²不能验证物理假设，也不能证明破坏强度。<\/p><p>理想模型中，其他量不变时跨距加倍使位移增至八倍；圆直径加倍使位移降至十六分之一。应解释真实树枝何时不满足这些预测。审查改变控制条件、独立抽样不足、伪重复和无依据推断。<\/p><h3>评估<\/h3><p>个人报告1500字，不含参考文献、表格和附录，建议占单元90%。报告内标准：问题与物理推理15%；设计与可重复性20%；数据分析25%；不确定度与批判评价25%；沟通与诚信15%。提交原始数据、可检查公式或代码、共享数据来源及帮助声明。口头检查建议占10%：解释一个计算、论证一个决策、指出一个改变解释的局限；物理推理、数据解释和批判判断等权。须采用本校评分尺度与规定。<\/p><h3>支持、人工智能与修订<\/h3><p>提供引导电子表格、换算例题和模板，同时提供开放分析路径。拓展关注几何敏感性、不确定度传播或不同模型。因无法实践而使用模拟数据时，实践能力仍需另行取证。 Jonathan began with one practical investigation of sticks and developed two learning pathways: one for fifteen-year-old learners, and one for first-year undergraduates. The project grew through repeated revisions to the teaching materials, activities, navigation, translations and avatar guidance. Those revisions showed that a change to one part could disrupt another, so shared components and checks across languages and devices need to come earlier. Working with AI accelerated drafting and development, but also reinforced the need for human judgement, subject checks and accessibility review. The main lesson is to establish the learners’ needs and agree outcomes with stakeholders before building too much. This is a self-directed prototype based on a fictional brief, not a validated course. The next steps are stakeholder and subject review, keyboard and screen-reader testing, mobile and browser checks, native-speaker review of translations and recordings, and a supervised rehearsal of the practical work.
